abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is one of the most prevalent and pharmaco-resistant forms of focal epilepsy in adults. The precise cellular and network mechanisms underlying TLE progression remain elusive. Animal models are essential for studying molecular and cellular mechanisms of TLE; however, widely used models largely rely on acute seizure induction and fail to recapitulate the gradual, progressive course of human TLE. Here, we present an optogenetic kindling mouse model of TLE, in which repeated stimulation induces a progressive increase in seizure susceptibility. This mouse model exhibits prominent TLE phenotypes, including robust hippocampal epileptiform activity, behavioral seizures, emotional changes, reactive astrogliosis, and impaired hippocampal learning and memory. Moreover, hippocampal synaptic analyses of this model revealed altered synaptic transmission and plasticity, without structural changes in excitatory or inhibitory synapses or overt cell death. These findings demonstrate that progressive epileptogenesis, synaptic dysfunction and TLE-associated phenotypes can develop independently of structural remodeling or overt cell death. This model provides a platform for investigating the synaptic mechanisms underlying TLE-associated synaptopathy.
